nodes.name: Composite minimization problem
nodes.statement: The composite minimization problem \begin{align} \min_{\mathbf{x}\in \mathds{R}^d}~ f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}) \end{align} has drawn a lot of recent attention due to its ubiquity in machine learning and statistical applications.
nodes.statement_short: Minimize $f+g$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$, with $f$ a smooth loss and $g$ a nonsmooth regularizer.

nodes.name: Composite minimization objective
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{x}\in \mathds{R}^d}~ f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x})
nodes.label: com_min

nodes.name: Finite-sum loss
nodes.statement: f(\mathbf{x}) := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(\mathbf{x})
nodes.label: finitesum

nodes.name: Lasso, logistic regression, boosting and SVM as composite problems
nodes.statement: We list below some popular examples under this framework. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=20pt,topsep=3pt,itemsep=3pt] \item Lasso: least squares loss $f_i(\mathbf{x}) = (y_i - \mathbf{a}_i^\top \mathbf{x})^2$ and $\ell_1$ norm regularizer $g(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x}\|_1$; \item Logistic regression: logistic loss $f_i = \log(1+\exp(-y_i \mathbf{a}_i^\top \mathbf{x}_i))$; \item Boosting: exponential loss $f_i(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(-y_i \mathbf{a}_i^\top\mathbf{x})$; \item Support vector machines: hinge loss $f_i(\mathbf{x}) =\max\{0, 1-y_i\mathbf{a}_i^\top \mathbf{x}\}$ and (squared) $\ell_2$ norm regularizer $g(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x}\|_2^2$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Lasso, logistic regression, boosting and SVMs as instances of loss plus regularizer.

nodes.name: Proper closed extended real-valued function; domain
nodes.statement: Throughout, $h:\mathds{R}^d \to (-\infty, +\infty]$ denotes an extended real-valued function that is proper and closed, {i.e.}\xspace, its domain $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h := \{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) < +\infty \}$ is nonempty and its sublevel set $\{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) \leq \alpha \}$ is closed for all $\alpha\in\mathds{R}$.
differentia: its domain $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h := \{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) < +\infty \}$ is nonempty
its sublevel set $\{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) \leq \alpha \}$ is closed for all $\alpha\in\mathds{R}$
nodes.statement_short: $h$ is proper (nonempty domain $\mathrm{dom}\,h$) and closed (closed sublevel sets).

nodes.name: Subdifferential and critical point
nodes.statement: The Frech\'et subdifferential $\hat\partial h$ of $h$ at $\mathbf{x}\in\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h$ is the set of $\mathbf{u}$ such that \begin{align} \liminf_{\mathbf{z}\neq\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}\to\mathbf{x}} \frac{h(\mathbf{z}) - h(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{u}^\top(\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x})}{\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|} \geq 0, \end{align} while the (limiting) subdifferential $\partial h$ at $\mathbf{x}\in\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h$ is the ``closure'' of $\hat\partial h$: \begin{align} \{ \mathbf{u}: \exists \mathbf{x}^k \to \mathbf{x}, h(\mathbf{x}^k) \to h(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{u}^k \in \hat{\partial} h(\mathbf{x}^k), \mathbf{u}^k \to \mathbf{u} \}. \end{align} The critical points of $h$ are $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h := \{ \mathbf{x}: \mathbf{0}\in\partial h(\mathbf{x}) \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fréchet subdifferential via a liminf condition, limiting subdifferential as its closure, critical points where $0\in\partial h$.
nodes.label: def:sub

nodes.name: Frechet subdifferential condition
nodes.statement: \liminf_{\mathbf{z}\neq\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}\to\mathbf{x}} \frac{h(\mathbf{z}) - h(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{u}^\top(\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x})}{\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|} \geq 0,

nodes.name: Limiting subdifferential
nodes.statement: \{ \mathbf{u}: \exists \mathbf{x}^k \to \mathbf{x}, h(\mathbf{x}^k) \to h(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{u}^k \in \hat{\partial} h(\mathbf{x}^k), \mathbf{u}^k \to \mathbf{u} \}.

nodes.name: Subdifferential agrees with usual notions
nodes.statement: When $h$ is continuously differentiable or convex, the subdifferential $\partial h$ and the set of critical points $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h$ coincide with the usual notions.
conclusions: the subdifferential $\partial h$ and the set of critical points $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h$ coincide with the usual notions

nodes.name: Nonemptiness or divergence of the subdifferential of a closed function
nodes.statement: For a closed function $h$, its subdifferential is either nonempty at any point in its domain or the subgradient diverges to some ``direction'' \cite[Corollary 8.10]{vari_ana}.
conclusions: its subdifferential is either nonempty at any point in its domain or the subgradient diverges to some ``direction''

nodes.name: Distance and projection
nodes.statement: The distance function {w.r.t.}\xspace a closed set $\Omega \subseteq \mathds{R}^d$ is defined as: \begin{align} \mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \min_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|, \end{align} while the metric projection onto $\Omega$ is defined as: \begin{align} \proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|, \end{align} where $\|\cdot\|$ is the usual Euclidean norm.
nodes.statement_short: Distance to a closed set $\Omega$ and the metric projection onto it, in the Euclidean norm.
nodes.label: def: distance

nodes.name: Distance function
nodes.statement: \mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \min_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,

nodes.name: Metric projection
nodes.statement: \proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,

nodes.name: Projection is single-valued iff the set is convex
nodes.statement: Note that $\proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x})$ is single-valued for all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d$ if and only if $\Omega$ is convex.
conclusions: $\proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x})$ is single-valued for all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d$ if and only if $\Omega$ is convex

nodes.name: Proximal map
nodes.statement: The proximal map of a closed and proper function $h$ is (with parameter $\eta > 0$): \begin{align} \prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{z}\in \mathds{R}^d} h(\mathbf{z}) + \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\|^2. \end{align} Occasionally, we will write $\prox[]{h}$ instead of $\prox[1]{h}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{prox}^\eta_h(x)=\arg\min_z h(z)+\|z-x\|^2/(2\eta)$.
nodes.label: def:prox_map

nodes.name: Proximal map formula
nodes.statement: \prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{z}\in \mathds{R}^d} h(\mathbf{z}) + \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\|^2.

nodes.name: Proximal map of an indicator is the projection
nodes.statement: Clearly, for the indicator function $ h(\mathbf{x}) = \iota_\Omega(\mathbf{x})$, which takes the value 0 for $\mathbf{x}\in \Omega$ and $\infty$ otherwise, its proximal map (with any $\eta > 0$) reduces to the metric projection $\proj{\Omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: The proximal map of the indicator $\iota_\Omega$ is the metric projection onto $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Well-definedness of the proximal map
nodes.statement: If $h$ decreases slower than a quadratic function (in particular, when $h$ is bounded below), then its proximal map is well-defined for all (small) $\eta$ \cite{vari_ana}.
assumptions: $h$ decreases slower than a quadratic function (in particular, when $h$ is bounded below)
conclusions: its proximal map is well-defined for all (small) $\eta$

nodes.name: Proximal map of convex function is a singleton
nodes.statement: If $h$ is convex, then its proximal map is always a singleton while for nonconvex $h$, the proximal map can be set-valued.
conclusions: its proximal map is always a singleton

nodes.name: Proximal map as a selection
nodes.statement: In the latter case we will also abuse the notation $\prox{h}(\mathbf{x})$ for an arbitrary element from that set.
nodes.definiendum: selection of a set-valued proximal map

nodes.name: Nonexpansiveness of the proximal map
nodes.statement: For convex functions, the proximal map is nonexpansive: \begin{align} \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \|\prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) - \prox{h}(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|, \end{align} while for nonconvex functions this may not hold everywhere.
conclusions: the proximal map is nonexpansive

nodes.name: Nonexpansiveness inequality
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \|\prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) - \prox{h}(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|,
nodes.label: eq:ne

nodes.name: Proximal gradient algorithm
nodes.statement: The proximal map is the key component of the proximal gradient algorithm \cite{FukushimaMine81} ({a.k.a.}\xspace forward-backward splitting): \begin{align} \forall\,t = 0, 1, \ldots, \quad \mathbf{x}(t+1) = \prox[\eta]{g}\big(\mathbf{x}(t) - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{x}(t))\big), \end{align} where $\nabla f$ is the (sub)gradient of $f$, and $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may change with $t$).
input: $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may  change with $t$)
nodes.statement_short: Forward-backward splitting: a gradient step on $f$ followed by the proximal map of $g$, iterated.

nodes.name: Proximal gradient iteration
nodes.statement: \forall\,t = 0, 1, \ldots, \quad \mathbf{x}(t+1) = \prox[\eta]{g}\big(\mathbf{x}(t) - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{x}(t))\big),
nodes.label: eq:pg

nodes.name: O(1/t) convergence of proximal gradient
nodes.statement: It is known that when $f$ is convex with $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient and $0 < \eta < 2/L$, then $F_t := f(\mathbf{x}(t))+g(\mathbf{x}(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$ and $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to some minimizer $\mathbf{x}^*$.
conclusions: $F_t := f(\mathbf{x}(t))+g(\mathbf{x}(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$
$\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to some minimizer $\mathbf{x}^*$
nodes.statement_short: For convex $f$ with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $\eta<2/L$, proximal gradient converges at rate $O(1/t)$.

nodes.name: Accelerated proximal gradient O(1/t^2) rate
nodes.statement: Accelerated versions \cite{FISTA,Nesterov13} where $F_t$ converges at the faster rate $O(1/t^2)$ are also well-known.
conclusions: $F_t$ converges at the faster rate $O(1/t^2)$

nodes.name: Convergence of proximal gradient under the KL inequality
nodes.statement: Recently, \cite{prox_alter_linear} proved that $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to a critical point even for nonconvex $f$ and nonconvex and nonsmooth $g$ as long as together they satisfy a certain K\L\xspace inequality.
assumptions: together they satisfy a certain K\L\xspace inequality
conclusions: $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to a critical point

nodes.name: Composite problem (P)
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d} F(\mathbf{x}), \quad \mbox{ where } \quad F(\mathbf{x}) = f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}). \tag{P}
nodes.label: compmin

nodes.name: Model parallel system with p machines
nodes.statement: We consider a \textbf{model} parallel system with $p$ machines in total, and decompose the $d$ model parameters into $p$ disjoint groups.
nodes.statement_short: $p$ machines; the $d$ parameters split into $p$ disjoint groups.

nodes.name: Block decomposition and partial gradients
nodes.statement: Formally, consider the decomposition $ \mathds{R}^d = \mathds{R}^{d_1} \times \mathds{R}^{d_2} \times\cdots\times\mathds{R}^{d_p}$, and denote $x_i$ and $\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}): \mathds{R}^d \to \mathds{R}^{d_i}$ as the $i$-th component of $\mathbf{x}$ and $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: $x_i$ and $\nabla_i f$ are the $i$-th blocks of $\mathbf{x}$ and $\nabla f$ under $\mathbb{R}^d=\prod_i\mathbb{R}^{d_i}$.

nodes.name: Local full model access
nodes.statement: The $i$-th machine is responsible for updating the component $x_i\in\mathds{R}^{d_i}$, and for the purpose of evaluating the partial gradient $\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x})$ we assume the $i$-th machine also has access to a local, full model parameter $\mathbf{x}^i\in\mathds{R}^d$.
nodes.statement_short: Machine $i$ updates block $x_i$ and keeps a local full copy $\mathbf{x}^i$ of the model.

nodes.name: Bounded Below
nodes.statement: The function $F \!=\! f+g$ is bounded below.
nodes.label: assum:bb

nodes.name: Smooth
nodes.statement:
The gradient $
abla f$ of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous:  egin{align}  orall \mathbf{x},  orall \mathbf{y}, ~ \| 
abla f(\mathbf{x}) - 
abla f(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq L \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\nabla f$ is $L$-Lipschitz.
nodes.label: assum:smooth

nodes.name: Lipschitz gradient
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \| \nabla f(\mathbf{x}) - \nabla f(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq L \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|.

nodes.name: Separable
nodes.statement: The function $g$ is closed and separable, {i.e.}\xspace, $g(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^{p} g_i(x_i)$.
nodes.label: assum:separable

nodes.name: Quadratic upper bound (descent lemma)
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~f(\mathbf{x}) \leq f(\mathbf{y}) + \langle \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}, \nabla f(\mathbf{y}) \rangle + \tfrac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|^2.
nodes.label: eq:qb

nodes.name: m-PAPG
nodes.statement: Formally, the $t$-th iteration on machine $i$ can be written as: \begin{equation} \tag{\textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace} \left\{ \begin{aligned} \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases} , \\ \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big), \\ \mbox{(global)}\quad \mathbf{x}(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big). \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation} That is, machine $i$ only performs its update operator at its active clocks. The local full model $\mathbf{x}^i(t)$ assembles all components from other machines, and is possibly a delayed version of the global model $\mathbf{x}(t)$, which assembles the most up-to-date component in each machine. Note that the global model is introduced for our analysis, and is not accessible in a real implementation. More specifically, $\tau_j^i(t) \leq t$ models the communication delay among machines: when machine $i$ conducts its $t$-th update it only has access to $x_j(\tau_j^i(t))$, a delayed version of the component $x_j(t)$ on the $j$-th machine. We refer to the above algorithm as \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace (for \textbf{m}odel parallel, \textbf{P}artially \textbf{A}synchronous, \textbf{P}roximal \textbf{G}radient).
nodes.statement_short: Model-parallel partially asynchronous proximal gradient: machine $i$ applies a proximal gradient step to block $x_i$ at its active clocks, using a delayed local copy of the model.

nodes.name: Separable proximal map
nodes.statement: \prox{g}(\mathbf{x}) = \big( \prox{g_1}(x_1),~ \ldots~,~ \prox{g_p}(x_p) \big).

nodes.name: Machine update operator
nodes.statement: x_i \gets \prox{g_i}(x_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i)).
nodes.label: update_op

nodes.name: Active clocks T_i
nodes.statement: To define the latter, consider a global clock shared by all machines and denote $T_i$ as the set of active clocks when machine $i$ performs an update.

nodes.name: m-PAPG iteration
nodes.statement: \tag{\textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace} \left\{ \begin{aligned} \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases} , \\ \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big), \\ \mbox{(global)}\quad \mathbf{x}(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big). \end{aligned} \right.
nodes.label: mspg_formulation

nodes.name: Update block at active clocks
nodes.statement: x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases}
nodes.statement_short: Machine $i$ keeps $x_i$ unchanged off its active clocks and takes a proximal gradient step on them.

nodes.name: Assemble delayed local model
nodes.statement: \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big)
nodes.statement_short: The local full model collects possibly delayed copies of every block.

nodes.name: Communication delays tau
nodes.statement: More specifically, $\tau_j^i(t) \leq t$ models the communication delay among machines: when machine $i$ conducts its $t$-th update it only has access to $x_j(\tau_j^i(t))$, a delayed version of the component $x_j(t)$ on the $j$-th machine.
nodes.statement_short: $\tau_j^i(t)\le t$ is the clock of the copy of block $j$ that machine $i$ sees at time $t$.

nodes.name: Bounded Delay
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall j, \forall t, ~0 \leq t-\tau_j^i(t) \leq s$, $\tau_i^i(t) \equiv t$.
nodes.statement_short: Delays are at most $s$ clocks, and each machine sees its own block without delay.
nodes.label: assum:delay

nodes.name: Frequent Update
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall t, T_i \cap \{t, t+1, \cdots, t+s\} \ne \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_short: Every machine updates at least once in every window of $s+1$ clocks.
nodes.label: assum:skip

nodes.name: m-PAPG with s = 0 is synchronous proximal gradient
nodes.statement: Clearly, when $s = 0$ ({i.e.}\xspace, no delay), \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace reduces to the fully synchronous, model parallel proximal gradient algorithm.

nodes.name: Positive part
nodes.statement: Recall that $(t)_+ = \max\{t, 0\}$ is the positive part of $t$.

nodes.name: Inconsistency bound between local and global models
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:delay} hold, then the global model $\mathbf{x}(t)$ and the local models $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ satisfy: \begin{align} \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. \end{align}
conclusions: \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|.
nodes.statement_short: Local and global models differ by at most the sum of the last $s$ successive global differences.
nodes.label: thm:incon

nodes.name: Local-global inconsistency bounds
nodes.statement: \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|.
nodes.label: incon_bound

nodes.name: Proof of the inconsistency bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &=\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\|\mathbf{x}(k'+1) - \mathbf{x}(k') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^{i}(t) - \mathbf{x}^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality over delayed blocks, the bounded delay, and Cauchy-Schwarz; the second bound is analogous.

nodes.name: Bound global-local gap
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &=\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\|\mathbf{x}(k'+1) - \mathbf{x}(k') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|x(t)-x^i(t)\|^2$ by telescoping, bounded delay and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Bound local successive differences
nodes.statement: Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^{i}(t) - \mathbf{x}^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.

nodes.name: Square summability of m-PAPG iterates
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip} hold. If the step size $\eta \in \left(0, \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}s)}\right)$, then the sequence generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace is square summable, {i.e.}\xspace \begin{align} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 < \infty. \end{align} In particular, $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| = 0$ and $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| = 0$.

In particular, $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| = 0$ and  $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| = 0$.

nodes.name: Step size rule discussion
nodes.statement: Our bound on the step size $\eta$ is natural: If $s = 0$, {i.e.}\xspace, there is no asynchronism then we recover the standard step size rule $\eta < 1/L$ (we can increase $\eta$ by another factor of 2, had convexity on $g$ been assumed). As staleness $s$ increases, we need a smaller step size to ``damp'' the system to still ensure convergence. The factor $\sqrt{p}$ is another measurement of the degree of ``dependency'' among worker machines: Indeed, we can reduce $\sqrt{p}$ to $\sqrt{\sum_i L_i^2} / L$, where $L_i$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\nabla_i f$ ({cf.}\xspace \eqref{eq:Lip}).
nodes.statement_short: For $s=0$ the step size recovers $\eta<1/L$; staleness forces smaller steps; $\sqrt{p}$ can be refined via blockwise Lipschitz constants.

nodes.name: Criticality criterion
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{x}^*$ be a limit point of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$. By \Cref{def:sub} it suffices to exhibit a sequence $\mathbf{x}(k)$ satisfying\footnote{Technically, from \Cref{def:sub} we should have the Frech\'et subdifferential $\hat{\partial} F$ in \cref{crit_want}, however, a standard argument allows us to use the more convenient subdifferential \cite[Proposition 8.7]{vari_ana}.} \begin{align} \mathbf{x}(k) \to \mathbf{x}^*, ~ F(\mathbf{x}(k)) \to F(\mathbf{x}^*), ~ \mathbf{0} \leftarrow \mathbf{u}(k) \in \partial F(\mathbf{x}(k)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: By the subdifferential definition it suffices to find iterates with converging values and vanishing subgradients.

nodes.statement: Let us first construct the subgradient sequence $\mathbf{u}(k)$. Consider machine $i$ and any $\hat t \in T_i$, the optimality condition of \cref{update_exp} gives \begin{flalign} u_i( \hat t+1) := -\tfrac{1}{\eta} \left[x_i(\hat t+1) - x_i(\hat t) + \eta \nabla_{i} f\big(\mathbf{x}^i(\hat t)\big)\right] \in \partial g_i(x_i( \hat t+1)). \end{flalign}
nodes.statement_short: At an active clock, prox optimality yields a subgradient $u_i$ of $g_i$.

Next we verify the function value convergence in \cref{crit_want}. The challenge here is that the component function $g$ is only closed, hence may not be continuous.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a convergent subsequence; the difficulty is that $g$ is only closed.

nodes.name: Apply prox inequality at the limit

nodes.name: Limsup on active clocks
nodes.statement: Observe from \Cref{thm:limitcon} that \begin{align*} \lim_{m\to\infty} \max_{t \in [t_m-s, t_m + s]} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^*\| = 0, \qquad \lim_{m\to\infty} \max_{t \in [t_m-s, t_m + s]} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^*\| = 0. \end{align*} By \Cref{assum:skip}, $[t_m -s, t_m + s] \cap T_i \ne \emptyset$ for all $i$. Then using the Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla f$ we deduce from \cref{uniform} that \begin{align} \limsup_{m \to \infty} \max_{t\in[t_m-s, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq g_i(x_i^*). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Iterates in windows around $t_m$ converge, giving limsup of $g_i$ at most $g_i(x_i^*)$ on active clocks.

nodes.name: Limsup on windows
nodes.statement: Since each machine updates at least once during $[t_m-s, t_m]$, let $\hat t_m$ be the largest element of $[t_m-s, t_m] \cap T_i$. Also notice that each machine $i$ only updates at its active clocks $T_i$, it then follows that \begin{align*} \max_{t\in[t_m, t_m+s]} g_i(x_i(t+1)) = \max_{t\in[\hat t_m, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq \max_{t\in[t_m -s, t_m+s] \cap T_i} g_i(x_i(t+1)), \end{align*} and hence by \eqref{eq:func_con} \begin{align} \limsup_{m \to \infty} \max_{t\in[t_m, t_m+s]} g_i(x_i(t+1)) \leq g_i(x_i^*). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Extend the limsup bound to all clocks in $[t_m,t_m+s]$.

nodes.name: Choose k_m
nodes.statement: To complete the proof, choose any $k_m\in [t_m, t_m+s]$. Since $\mathbf{x}(t_m) \to \mathbf{x}^*$, \Cref{thm:limitcon} implies that \begin{align} \mathbf{x}(k_m) \to \mathbf{x}^*. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Pick $k_m$ in the window; $x(k_m)\to x^*$.

nodes.name: Function values converge
nodes.statement: From \cref{eq: usc} we know for all $i$, $\limsup\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) \leq g_i(x_i^*)$. On the other hand, it follows from the closedness of the function $g_i$ ({cf.}\xspace \Cref{assum:separable}) that $\liminf\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) \geq g_i(x_i^*)$, thus in fact $ \lim\limits_{m\to\infty} g_i(x_i(k_m)) = g_i(x_i^*) $. Since $f$ is continuous, we know \begin{align} \lim_{m\to \infty} F(\mathbf{x}(k_m)) = \lim_{m\to \infty} f(\mathbf{x}(k_m)) + \sum_i g_i(x_i(k_m)) = F(\mathbf{x}^*). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Closedness gives the matching liminf, so $F(x(k_m))\to F(x^*)$.

nodes.name: Conclude criticality
nodes.statement: Combining \cref{crit_1}, \cref{crit_2} and \cref{crit_3} we know from \Cref{def:sub} that $\mathbf{x}^* \in \mathop{\mathrm{crit}}{F}$.
nodes.statement_short: All three conditions hold, so $x^*$ is critical.

nodes.name: Existence of limit points
nodes.statement: We note that the existence of limit points can be guaranteed, for instance, if $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is bounded or the sublevel set $\{\mathbf{x} ~|~ F(\mathbf{x}) \le \alpha \}$ is bounded for all $\alpha \in \mathds{R}$.

nodes.statement: For every $\alpha > 0$, there exist $\delta ,\kappa>0$ such that for all $\mathbf{x}$ with $f(\mathbf{x}) \leq \alpha$ and $\|\mathbf{x} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{x} - \nabla f(\mathbf{x}))\| \leq \delta$, \begin{align} \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{x}) \leq \kappa \|\mathbf{x} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{x} - \nabla f(\mathbf{x}))\|, \end{align} where recall that $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F$ is the set of critical points of $F$.

nodes.name: Relation to the Luo-Tseng error bound
nodes.statement: \Cref{eq:eb} is a proximal extension of the Luo-Tseng error bound \cite{LuoTseng93} where $g$ is the indicator function of a closed convex set.

nodes.name: Prototypic function satisfying the error bound
nodes.statement: A prototypic convex function $F$ satisfying \eqref{eq:eb} is the following: \begin{align} F(\mathbf{x}) = f(A\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}), \end{align} where $f$ is strongly convex ({i.e.}\xspace, $f-\tfrac{\mu}{2}\|\cdot\|^2$ is convex for some $\mu > 0$), $A$ is a linear map, and $g$ is either an indicator function of a convex set \cite{LuoTseng93} or the $\ell_p$ norm for $p\in [1,2]\cup\{\infty\}$ \cite{EB2015}.
nodes.statement_short: $F(x)=f(Ax)+g(x)$ with strongly convex $f$ and $g$ an indicator of a convex set or an $\ell_p$ norm satisfies the error bound.

nodes.statement: F(\mathbf{x}) = f(A\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}),

nodes.name: Error bound equivalent to restricted strong convexity and quadratic growth
nodes.statement: In fact, for convex functions $F$ taking such form, the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is recently shown to be equivalent to the following conditions \cite{DrusvyatskiyLewis16,Zhang2016}: \begin{align*} \text{Restricted strong convexity}: ~ &\inner{ \mathbf{x} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathbf{x} - \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{x})} \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}), \\ \text{Quadratic growth}: ~ &F(\mathbf{x}) - F^* \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}), \end{align*} where $F^*$ is the minimum value of $F$ and $\mu>0$ is a constant.
assumptions: for convex functions $F$ taking such form
conclusions: the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is recently shown to be equivalent to the following conditions
nodes.statement_short: For such $F$, the error bound is equivalent to restricted strong convexity and to quadratic growth.

nodes.name: Nonconvex function satisfying the error bound
nodes.statement: In general, the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is not exclusive to convex functions. For instance, it holds for $f(\mathbf{x})= \tfrac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{x}\|^2$ and any function $g$ that has a unique global minimizer at $0$ (such as the cardinality function $g(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x}\|_0$).
nodes.statement_short: $f=\|x\|^2/2$ with any $g$ uniquely minimized at 0 (e.g. $\ell_0$) satisfies the error bound.

nodes.name: First inequality by summation
nodes.statement: The first inequality is obtained by summing the inequality \cref{eq: progress} over $t, t+1, \cdots, t+s$. So we need only prove the second inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the one-step progress bound; only the second inequality remains.

nodes.name: Introduce last-update points
nodes.statement: Let us introduce some notations to simplify the proof. For each machine $i$ let $t_i$ be the largest clock in $[t, t+s] \cap T_i$, and denote \begin{align} \mathbf{z} &= \big(x_1(t_1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p)\big) \\ \mathbf{z}^+ &= \big(x_1(t_1+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p+1)\big) = \big(x_1(t+s+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t+s+1)\big), \end{align} where the last equality is due to the maximality of each $t_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $t_i$, $\mathbf{z}$ and $\mathbf{z}^+$ from the last update clocks.

nodes.name: Prox optimality
nodes.statement: From the optimality condition of the proximal map $z^+_i = \prox{g_i}(z_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t_i)))$ we deduce \begin{align} \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) \in \partial g_i (z_i^+). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Subgradient of $g_i$ at $z_i^+$.

nodes.name: Descent and convexity bounds
nodes.statement: Since the gradient of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous and the function $g$ is convex, we obtain \begin{align*} f(\mathbf{z}^+) - f(\bar\mathbf{z}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i - \bar z_i, \nabla_i f(\bar\mathbf{z})\rangle + \frac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \bar\mathbf{z}\|^2, \\ g(\mathbf{z}^+) - g(\bar\mathbf{z}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i - \bar z_i, \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) \rangle, \end{align*} where we define $\bar \mathbf{z} := \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{z})$, {i.e.}\xspace, the projection of $\mathbf{z}$ onto the set of critical points of $F$, and the last inequality follows from \cref{eq:subgrad}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $f$ and $g$ increments relative to the projection $\bar z$.

nodes.name: Add the bounds
nodes.statement:
Adding up the above two inequalities we obtain  egin{align*} F(&\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* - 	frac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ -  ar\mathbf{z}\|^2 \le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i -  ar z_i, 
abla_i f( ar\mathbf{z}) + \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))angle \ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \sum_{i=1}^{p} [\|z_i^+ - z_i\| + \|z_i -  ar z_i\|] [\|
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) - 
abla_i f( ar\mathbf{z})\| + \eta^{-1} \|z_i - z_i^+\|] \ &\overset{\mathrm{(ii)}}{\le} \sum_{i=1}^{p} 4\left[ \|z_i^+ - z_i\|^2 + \|z_i -  ar z_i\|^2 + \eta^{-2} \|z_i^+ - z_i\|^2 + \|
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) - 
abla_i f( ar\mathbf{z})\|^2 ight] \ &\le 4\left[ \| ar\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (1+\eta^{-2}) \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{p} L^2 \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) -  ar\mathbf{z}\|^2 ight], \end{align*} where (i) is due to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the triangle inequality, (ii) is due to the elementary inequality $(a+b)(c+d) \leq 4(a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2)$, and the last inequality is due to the $L$-Lipschitz continuity of $
abla f$.
nodes.statement_short: Add and bound via Cauchy-Schwarz and $(a+b)(c+d)\le4(a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2)$.

nodes.name: Gap bound
nodes.statement: Using again the triangle inequality we obtain from the above inequality that \begin{align} F(\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* &\le (L+4)\|\bar\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L+4+\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) - \mathbf{z}\|^2 \nonumber\\ \nonumber&\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{=} (L\!+\!4)\|\bar\mathbf{z} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 \!+\! \sum_{i=1}^{p} [(L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}})\|x_i(t_i\!+\!1) \!-\! x_i(t_i)\|^2 \!+\! 4L^2\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2],\\ &\overset{\mathrm{(ii)}}{\leq} (L\!+\!4)\|\bar\mathbf{z} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t+s+1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2, \end{align} where (i) is due to our definition of $\mathbf{z}$ and $\mathbf{z}^+$ in \eqref{eq:z} and \eqref{eq:z2}, and (ii) is due to the fact that $t_i \in [t, t+s]$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $F(z^+)-F^*$ by $\|\bar z-z\|^2$, $B(t+s+1)$ and local deviations.

nodes.name: Lower bound block steps
nodes.statement:
We next bound the terms $\| ar\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}\|^2$ and $\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2$. First, note that  egin{align*} \| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\| &= \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\ge \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\quad - \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))) - \prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) \| \ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\ge} \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) - x_i(t_i)\| - \eta L \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|, \end{align*} where (i) follows from the non-expansiveness of $\prox{g}$ (recall that $g$ is convex) and the $L$-Lipschitz continuity of $
abla f$.
nodes.statement_short: Use nonexpansiveness of the prox to compare steps.

nodes.name: Sum over blocks
nodes.statement: Rearranging the above inequality and summing over all $i$, we obtain \begin{align} \nonumber \|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z}- \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{z})) - \mathbf{z}\|^2 &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \left[\| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\| + \eta L \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\| \right]^2 \\ &\le 2\sum_{i=1}^p \left[\| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\||^2 + \eta^2 L^2 \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2 \right]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the proximal residual at $z$.

nodes.name: Bound local deviations
nodes.statement:
The last term $\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2$ can be further bounded as follows:  egin{align} 
onumber \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t_j) - x_j (	au_j^i (t_i))\|^2 \ &= \sum_{j=1}^p \Big\|\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \Big\|^2 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^p \Big[\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \| \Big]^2 
onumber\ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \sum_{j=1}^p 2s \sum_{k= t-s}^{t+s-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|^2 
onumber\ 
onumber &= 2s \sum_{k=t-s}^{t+s-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|^2 \ & \leq 2s [B(t) + B(t+s+1)], \end{align} where (i) is due to the fact that $t_j \in [t, t+s]$ and $	au_j^i(t_i) \in [t-s, t+s]$.
nodes.statement_short: Local deviations bounded by $2s[B(t)+B(t+s+1)]$.

nodes.name: Combine residual bounds
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:proxb} and \eqref{eq:diff} we obtain \begin{align} \|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{z})) &- \mathbf{z}\|^2 \leq 2 B(t+s+1) + 4ps\eta^2 L^2 [B(t) + B(t+s+1)]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Residual bounded by $B$ terms.

nodes.name: Apply error bound
nodes.statement:
Thanks to \Cref{thm:limitcon}, we know for $t$ sufficiently large, $\|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z})) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\| \leq \eta\delta$. Since the function $\eta \mapsto  rac{1}{\eta}\|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z})) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|$ is monotonically decreasing \cite{Sra12}, we can apply the error bound condition in \Cref{assum:eb} for $\eta < 1$ and $t$ sufficiently large, and obtain  egin{align} \| ar\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 \le \kappa \|\mathbf{z} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{z} - 
abla f(\mathbf{z}))\|^2 \le \kappa \eta^{-2} \|\mathbf{z} - \prox{g}(\mathbf{z} - \eta
abla f(\mathbf{z}))\|^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For large $t$ the residual is small; monotonicity in $\eta$ lets the error bound apply.

nodes.name: Final combination
nodes.statement: Finally, combining \eqref{eq:Fgap}, \eqref{eq:diff}, \eqref{eq:pb} and \eqref{eq:projdist} we arrive at: \begin{align} \nonumber F(\mathbf{x}(t\!+\!s\!+\!1)) - F^* &= F(\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* \\ \nonumber&\le (L\!+\!4)\|\bar\mathbf{z} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t\!+\!s\!+\!1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2,\\ &\le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t), \end{align} where the coefficients are \begin{align} a_\eta &= L+4+8psL^2 + 4ps\kappa L^2(L+4) + \tfrac{2}{\eta^2}(2+4\kappa+\kappa L), \\ b &= 8psL^2+4ps\kappa L^2(L+4). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine all bounds to get $A(t+s+1)\le a_\eta B(t+s+1)+bB(t)$.

nodes.name: Proof of periodic linear convergence via Tseng's Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: The two recursive relations in Lemma \ref{lemma: EB_2}, as shown in \cite[Lemma 4.5]{Tseng_linear_PAA}, easily imply the following convergence guarantee:
nodes.statement_short: Cite Tseng's Lemma 4.5: the two recursive relations imply linear decay every $s+1$ steps.

nodes.name: Periodic linear convergence under error bound
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:convex,assum:eb} hold. Then, there exists some $\eta_0 >0$ such that if $0<\eta<\eta_0$, then the sequences $\{A(t), B(t)\}$ generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace satisfy for all $r = 0, 1, 2, \cdots$ \begin{align} A(r (s+1)) \le C_1 (1-\gamma \eta)^{r}, ~B(r (s+1)) \le C_2 (1-\gamma \eta)^{r}, \end{align} where $C_1, C_2,\gamma<1/\eta$ are positive constants.
nodes.statement_short: For small step sizes, $A$ and $B$ decay by a factor $(1-\gamma\eta)$ every $s+1$ steps.

nodes.name: Global finite length implies local
nodes.statement: We first show that \cref{global_finite} implies \cref{local_finite}. Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|. \end{align*} Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|. \end{align*} The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the local finite length to the global one.

nodes.name: Recall local difference bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Sum over t
nodes.statement: Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Each global difference is counted at most $2s+1$ times.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity.

nodes.name: Reduce to global finite length
nodes.statement: By \Cref{thm:limitcon}, the limit points of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ coincide and are critical points of $F$. Thus, the only thing left to prove is the finite length property in \cref{global_finite}.

nodes.name: Limit set and prox inequality
nodes.statement: Since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is assumed to be bounded, the set of its limit points $\Omega$ is nonempty and compact. Summing \cref{usc} over all $i$ and set $\mathbf{z} \in \Omega$, we obtain \[ g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z}) - \frac{1}{2\eta} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{p}\inner{\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))}{\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)}. \]

nodes.name: F constant on the limit set
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \to 0$. Also, since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is bounded and $\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\to 0$ for all $i$, $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ are all bounded. we then take limsup on both sides and obtain that $\limsup_{t\to\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z})$. Together with the closedness of $g$ we further obtain that $\lim_{t\to\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = g(\mathbf{z})$. Note that $f$ is continuous, we thus conclude that $\lim_{t\to\infty} F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = F(\mathbf{z})$ for all $\mathbf{z}\in \Omega$. Note that $F(\mathbf{x}(t)) \downarrow F^*$. Thus for all $\mathbf{x}^* \in \Omega$, we have $F(\mathbf{x}^*) \equiv F^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Closedness of $g$ and continuity of $f$ show $F\equiv F^*$ on $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Apply KL
nodes.statement: Now fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Since $\Omega$ is compact, for $t$ sufficiently large we have $\mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}(t)) \leq \varepsilon$. We now have all ingredients to apply the K\L\xspace inequality in \Cref{def:KL}: for all sufficiently large $t$, \begin{flalign} \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1. \end{flalign}

nodes.name: Lyapunov decrease
nodes.statement: Since $\varphi$ is concave, we obtain \begin{flalign} \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) - \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) - F^*\big) \nonumber\\ &\ge \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) -F(\mathbf{x}(t+1))\big) \nonumber\\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge} \frac{\alpha \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|^2}{\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0})}, \end{flalign} where (i) follows from \Cref{assum:sd} and \cref{uKL}.

nodes.name: AM-GM split
nodes.statement: It is clear that the function $\varphi$ (composed with $F$) serves as a Lyapunov function. Using the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{ab} \le a + b$ we obtain from \cref{Lyapunov} that for $t$ sufficiently large, \begin{flalign*} 2\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le \tfrac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t,t+1} + \tfrac{1}{\delta}\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}), \end{flalign*} where $\delta > 0$ will be specified later.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\|\Delta x\|$ via $2\sqrt{ab}\le a+b$.

nodes.name: Sum with subdifferential bound
nodes.statement: Recalling the bound for $\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))$ in \cref{subdiff_bound}, and summing over $t$ from $m$ (sufficiently large) to $n$ gives: \begin{flalign*} 2\sum_{t=m}^{n}&\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t, t+1} + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{1}{\delta} \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \\ &\ovset{(i)}{\le} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L}{\delta} \sum_{k = (t-2s)_+}^t \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ &\le \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ &\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{t=m}^{n} \| \mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|, \end{flalign*} where (i) is due to \cref{subdiff_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $t$, telescope $\varphi$ and use the subdifferential bound.

nodes.name: Choose delta and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta = (2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)$ and rearranging gives \begin{flalign*} \sum_{t=m}^{n}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| &\le \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) \\ &\quad+ \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. \end{flalign*} Since the right-hand side is finite, let $n$ tend to infinity completes the proof for \cref{global_finite}.
nodes.statement_short: Absorb the sum into the left side; the partial sums stay bounded.

nodes.name: Proof of finite length under proximal Lipschitz
nodes.statement:
Using the elementary inequality $\|a\|^2 - \|b\|^2 \le 2\|a\|\|a - b\|$, we have for all $t$:  egin{flalign} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - &\mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)ight\|^2 
onumber\ &\le 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \left\|(\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)) - (\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1))ight\| 
onumber\ &\leq 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p}\left\|(x_i(t+1) - x_i(t)) - (x_i(t+2) - x_i(t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p} \left \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t)) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(ii)}{\le} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \left(\sum_{i=1}^{p} L_\eta \|\mathbf{x}^{i} (t) - \mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1)\| ight)
onumber\ &\ovset{(iii)}{\le} 2pL_\eta \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|, \end{flalign} where (i) is due to \Cref{assum:always} hence $t\in T_i$ for all $t$, (ii) follows from \Cref{assum:EL}, and (iii) is due to \eqref{eq:local_diff}. onumber \end{flalign} which after rearranging terms becomes  egin{flalign} (C - s - 1)\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{T-1}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|. 
onumber \end{flalign} Since the right hand side does not depend on $n$, letting $n$ tend to infinity we conclude  egin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|< \infty, \end{flalign} and the proof of the finite length property would be complete. onumber\ &\leq \left(1- rac{1}{r^2} ight) \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|^2,
onumber \end{flalign} if $\eta$ is small enough (recall that $L_\eta = o(1)$).
